transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... my wife actually suggested I come in. We've been having some disagreements lately. 

It's... it's just about some things I've noticed. She says her late meetings and these little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. But... I don't know. For the past year, they’ve just lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It’s... it just feels like there’s a private signal in them, you know? Like they're meant to tell me something she won’t just say directly. 

So... she wanted me to talk to someone about it. I guess that's why I'm here.

When your wife explains that these messages are just normal work communications, what do you think—is it possible she might be right, or are you quite certain that there's a hidden meaning regardless of what she says?

I hear what she says. But... no, I don't think she's right. 

It's been a year of this. The timing of it all... they just line up too precisely to be an accident. It doesn't feel like normal office stuff. It feels like a signal. That's... that's really all I can say about it.

Apart from these messages from your wife, have you noticed other signs or patterns—in other people's behavior, or in events around you—that also seem to have hidden meanings or feel intentionally directed at you?

No... not really. I haven't noticed anything like that with anyone else. 

It's... it's just the things with my wife. That's all.

If you were to imagine, hypothetically, that these messages from your wife really are just normal work communications with no hidden meaning—how would that change your understanding of the situation? Do you think that's even possible?

I... I don't know how to answer that. 

Hypothetically? I guess... I guess I'd just be wrong. But... I don't think I am. I know she says it's just normal office stuff, the late meetings, the wording in those messages. But... like I said, it's been a year. The way they line up... it's just too precise. It doesn't feel accidental. It feels like a private signal. Like she's trying to tell me something she won't just come out and say. 

So... no, I don't really think it's possible that it's just normal work stuff. It doesn't make sense any other way.

When you think about the possibility that you might be misinterpreting these messages—not that your wife is right, but that your own mind might be connecting things that aren't actually connected—how does that idea sit with you? Is it something you can consider, or does it feel impossible?

I... I don't really like thinking about it like that. 

Like I just said... I know she claims the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. But... I'm not just inventing this. For the past year, they've just lined up too precisely to be an accident. It's... it's a private signal. It's meant to tell me something she won't say directly. 

So... no. I don't think my mind is just connecting things that aren't there.
When you think about why your wife would be sending you these private signals through her messages—what do you believe her reason or purpose is? What is she trying to communicate to you?

I... I don't really know. 

I just... I don't know why she's doing it. I just know that she is. I haven't really... figured out what the point of it all is yet.

If several people you trust—your wife, a close friend, a family member—all told you that these messages are just normal work communications and that they don't see any hidden signals, would that make you reconsider your interpretation, or would you still believe the signals are there?

I... I don't know. 

I mean, I've told you. My wife already says that. She says it's just normal office stuff. The meetings, the... the wording in those texts. But... I don't know what to tell you. If they all said it... I'd still see what I see. 

It's been a year of this. The way things line up... it's just too precise. It's not an accident. It's a signal, even if they don't see it. She's trying to tell me something she won't just say. So... no. I wouldn't reconsider. I know what's there.

On a scale where 0 means you're absolutely certain these signals are real and there's no possibility you could be wrong, and 10 means you're open to the idea that you might be misinterpreting things—where would you place yourself right now?

I'd... probably say a zero. 

I know she says it's just normal office stuff. The meetings, the texts. But... I told you, it's been a year. It's too precise. It's not an accident. It's a signal. She's trying to tell me something she won't say. 

So... zero. I'm not wrong about this.
